Subject: Compliance packaging — can you outline blended pricing?

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a clearer view of how Redwood would price the compliance stack for a 6–12 month pilot that could expand to ~30M tokens/month in year 1. Specifically we need: audit log retention costs (30/90/365 days), an HSM seat vs per-usage KMS line item, and any data residency premiums for US-only deployment.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you provide a blended example that shows how a pilot credit + annual commit would amortize the HSM/license cost?
- Any flexibility on audit log retention pricing for pilot customers? We can commit to a PO for the pilot if terms look reasonable.

Appreciate a concise grid or example numbers — procurement wants something to compare against our incumbent.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform
MedScale Health

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short example and attached a spreadsheet that models three scenarios (pilot -> ramp -> steady state). High level summary below; details in the attached workbook (audit_pricing_breakdown.xlsx).

Summary (pilot -> yr1 steady):
- Audit logs: pilot (30-day retention) = $0.002/token of logged activity/day; move to 90-day = +70% incremental; 365-day = +220% incremental. For your pilot we can cap 30-day retention at a fixed monthly fee of $3k for the first 3 months to simplify billing.
- HSM/KMS: two options — seat-based (flat monthly seat $6k, recommended for high-key churn) vs usage-based KMS (per-1M ops $0.15). For your expected token mix, a blended amortization shows seat + throughput is ~18% cheaper at scale but requires commitment.
- Residency premium: US-only routing (single-region) + SOC2 log storage = 8–12% surcharge on affected units.

Concessions we can propose for pilot:
- One-time pilot credit: $20k applied to RPU/ingress or audit logs (non-refundable)
- HSM amortization: we can amortize up to 50% of the first 6 months of seat cost against the pilot credit for a 12-month committed conversion.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with a 10% mid-year safe harbor.

Next steps: if you want, Ben can sketch an amortization table that ties HSM seat vs per-call and shows the effective unit economics at 5M/10M/30M tokens/month. Also we can draft a short SOW with the pilot scope and milestone-based payments.

I put Ben and Laura on cc — Ben for the cost/finance view and Laura for the SOW/legal checklist.

—Mateo
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Compliance packaging — can you outline blended pricing? (amortization examples)

Alex / team — quick note with the amortization examples Mateo suggested. I expanded the spreadsheet with three sample volume points and two billing mixes:

A) Seat-heavy (HSM seat + standard audit rate) — includes 12-month seat amortization spread monthly. Example: 1 seat ($6k/mo) with pilot credit amortized 50% over first 6 months reduces effective seat cost to ~$3k/mo during conversion period.
B) Usage-heavy (per-op KMS + higher audit-retention marginals) — no commitment, higher per-op cost but zero seat amortization risk.

Pilot proposal (practical terms):
- Pilot length: 90 days production-style (with up to 60% of pilot volume billable; remainder covered by pilot credit).
- Pilot credit: $20,000 applied first to audit log billing, then to token-based invoices.
- HSM seat concession: 50% of seat for first 3 months covered by credit if you sign a 12-month conversion PO within 45 days of pilot end.
- Audit retention: 30-day retention capped at $3k/mo for first 3 months (overages billed monthly).

Flags / trade-offs to consider:
- If MedScale requires 365-day audit logs during pilot we can do it but it will materially increase storage egress and will need an amended PO for cost recovery.
- If you need guaranteed region-level isolation (private deployment) there is a setup fee and longer lead time.

If this looks aligned, Laura will spin a short SOW + term sheet. Alex — can you confirm the PO owner and an anticipated PO approval date?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Pricing and Commercials | Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo / Ben — this is helpful and a good starting point. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:

1) Can the pilot credit be broadened to cover initial integration hours (we estimate ~40 engineering hours to wire audit events into Redwood)? If Redwood can credit up to $5k of integration labor, procurement can move the PO through faster.
2) On HSM seat concession — can you confirm the exact conversion trigger? \"Sign a 12-month conversion PO within 45 days of pilot end\" works, but procurement prefers a 60-day window.
3) Final ask on audit retention: can you offer a stepped retention pricing (30d -> 120d -> 365d) with a smoother slope? The big jump at 90->365 is the blocker here.

If you can get the integration credit and extend to 60 days for conversion, I think we can get procurement to sign the pilot PO this week. Also please include a one-page SOW excerpt with milestones and acceptance criteria — we want that in the PO attachment.

Appreciate the quick turn — look forward to the SOW.

Best,
Alex
